product_overview: Makaan is a rental property and tenancy management platform focused on landlord/tenant workflows, consent-aware user accounts, and deposit/inspection dispute handling. It provides an advisory AI-assisted audit experience for tenancy evidence without moving money or making binding decisions.
core_goals: Provide reliable authentication and session management for landlords and tenants
Allow landlords to manage properties and create tenancies, and tenants to accept invitations
Support tenancy lifecycle records including inspections, AI audits, statements, claims, and disputes
Expose consent management and personal data export features aligned with privacy requirements
Offer service health/status visibility for operational monitoring
Ensure all tenancy-scoped actions are authorization-safe and advisory only, with no money movement

features.name: Health API
features.description: Provides a simple service health and configuration status endpoint for monitoring and operational checks.
user_flows: GET /api/health -> Receive 200 with ok, service, ai, evidence, and time status fields
GET /api/health when the service is healthy but one subsystem is degraded -> Receive 200 with status payload indicating the degraded mode
GET /api/health with an unavailable service or malformed request -> Receive an error response appropriate to the failure condition

features.name: Authentication API
features.description: Supports user registration, login, logout, and session retrieval with CSRF token issuance.
user_flows: POST /api/auth/register with valid email, password, name, role, and consent payload -> Receive 201 with created user object and csrfToken -> GET /api/auth/session -> Receive 200 with current user and csrfToken
POST /api/auth/login with valid email and password -> Receive 200 with user object and csrfToken -> POST /api/auth/logout with session cookie and matching CSRF token -> Receive 200 with ok true
POST /api/auth/register with an email that already exists -> Receive 409 conflict error
POST /api/auth/login with invalid credentials -> Receive 401 unauthorized response

features.name: User Account and Consent API
features.description: Lets authenticated users review and update consent preferences and export their personal data.
user_flows: GET /api/me/consents with a valid session -> Receive 200 with the active consent records array
POST /api/me/consents with a valid session and a purpose/granted update -> Receive 200 with the updated consent object
GET /api/me/export with a valid session -> Receive 200 with the user's complete data export as JSON
POST /api/me/consents without authentication or with an invalid session -> Receive an authentication error response

features.name: Property Management API
features.description: Allows authenticated users to list, create, view, update, and delete rental properties with landlord-only write controls.
user_flows: GET /api/properties with a valid session -> Receive 200 with the properties array for the current landlord or tenant
POST /api/properties with landlord property details -> Receive 201 with the created property object and optional warning
GET /api/properties/{id} for a property the caller can access -> Receive 200 with property details and optional warning
PATCH /api/properties/{id} with updated property fields as the landlord -> Receive 200 with the updated property object
DELETE /api/properties/{id} for a property with no active tenancies -> Receive 200 with ok true
GET /api/properties/{id} for an inaccessible or missing property -> Receive 404 Not Found
POST /api/properties with a tenant account or invalid payload -> Receive an authorization or validation error response

features.name: Tenancy and Dispute Management API
features.description: Manages the full tenancy lifecycle, including invitations, acceptance, inspections, AI audits, deposit statements, claims, disputes, and dispute resolution.
user_flows: POST /api/tenancies with propertyId, tenantEmail, startDate, endDate, depositPaise, and monthlyRentPaise as the landlord -> Receive 201 with the created tenancy object -> GET /api/tenancies/{id} -> Receive 200 with complete tenancy details
POST /api/tenancies/{id}/accept with a tenant session for an invited tenancy -> Receive 200 with the accepted tenancy object -> GET /api/tenancies -> Receive 200 with the tenant's tenancy list
POST /api/tenancies/{id}/inspections with stage, area, and notes -> Receive 201 with the inspection object -> POST /api/tenancies/{id}/audit -> Receive 200 with the audit object
GET /api/tenancies/{id}/statement with an authenticated tenancy member -> Receive 200 with the deposit statement object

POST /api/tenancies/{id}/claims with claimPaise and rationale from the landlord -> Receive 200 with the claim object -> POST /api/tenancies/{id}/disputes with a tenant reason -> Receive 200 with the dispute object -> POST /api/tenancies/{id}/disputes/{disputeId}/resolve with resolvedPaise and resolutionNotes -> Receive 200 with the resolved dispute object
POST /api/tenancies/{id}/close for an active tenancy -> Receive 200 with the closed tenancy object
POST /api/tenancies/{id}/accept for a user who is not the invited tenant or for a non-invited tenancy -> Receive an authorization or validation error response
POST /api/tenancies/{id}/audit without prior inspections or with invalid tenancy access -> Receive an error response indicating the audit cannot proceed
